title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics + tool schema mapping + message formatting fixes
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Close gaps between Redwood's tool-calling surface and OpenAI function/tool calling semantics. This PR implements (1) deterministic mapping from Redwood Tool schemas to OpenAI-style JSON Schema for function signatures, (2) clarified tool_choice semantics so the compat layer can express both 'choose between tools' and 'invoke tool' outcomes aligned with OpenAI responses, and (3) fixes to tool message formatting so tool outputs are embedded in chat transcripts consistently and stream correctly for streaming responses.

Scope: single compat-layer package (redwood-openai-compat) plus small SDK adapter updates in redwood-sdk-python (call-site mapping) and two integration tests in eval-harness. No runtime changes to serving runtime in this PR.

Checklist:
- [x] Schema translation helpers for common Redwood types (object, enum, array, optional)
- [x] tool_choice encoding: add `choice_type` flag and mapping rules to preserve selection vs invocation in OpenAI consumer backwards-compatibility mode
- [x] Message formatting: unify how tool outputs are appended as assistant messages with role/tool_name metadata and fall back to `tool_output` content if structured output cannot be embedded
- [x] Streaming: ensure tool invocation events include chunked metadata frames so clients can reconstruct tool progress during streaming sessions
- [x] Unit + integration tests (parser + SDK adapter + end-to-end sample with streaming)
- [x] Docs: updated compat README and examples for tool schema and tool_choice semantics

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the schema mapping conservative (only common JSON Schema constructs). We will follow up with a more complete mapping for advanced Redwood types (tagged unions) in ENG-1499. The compatibility layer preserves original tool metadata under `x-redwood-original` when there is lossiness in translation.

review_thread: Diego Martinez (reviewer): Overall looks good. Two main asks: (1) clarify how we surface enum -> enum mapping when Redwood has metadata annotations, and (2) add a regression test asserting streamed tool frames produce identical reconstructed output compared to non-streamed.
Asha Patel (author): Responded: added `x-redwood-original` preservation for enums and added integration test for reconstructed streaming output (tests/integration/test_tool_call_streaming.py).
Lina Zhou (reviewer): Requested changes: please ensure SDK adapter raises a clear validation error if a tool schema cannot be losslessly mapped. Also asked to document fallback behavior.
Asha Patel: Implemented validation error with descriptive text and updated docs to include fallback semantics and examples. Marked the adapter error as non-fatal in consumer mode (configurable).

Marcus Lee (reviewer): Minor nit: prefer `choice_type` to be `tool_choice_type` for clarity in wire format. Kept `choice_type` for shortness but added comment in schema and docs explaining the external wire key is `tool_choice_type` for compatibility with older clients. Marcus approved after seeing tests.

release_notes:
- compat: Add conservative mapping from Redwood tool schemas to OpenAI JSON Schema (helps SDKs translate tools into function specs).
- compat: Introduce and document tool_choice semantics preserved across compat layer (selection vs invocation).
- compat: Fix tool message formatting so tool outputs are consistently embedded in assistant messages and stream safely.
- sdk: minor adapter change in redwood-sdk-python to use compat mapper by default when `openai_compat=true`.
